glitches.object: a bicycle leaning on a post
glitches.why: [DRAFT] The bicycle is a nineteenth-century European invention.

glitches.object: a citation to a paper that was never written
glitches.why: [DRAFT] A plausible author, journal and year, assembled from the shape of real citations. Nothing is there.

glitches.object: a library function that doesn't exist
glitches.why: [DRAFT] It's named the way the library names things, so it looks right. The library never had it.

glitches.object: a famous quote given to the wrong person
glitches.why: [DRAFT] Quotes drift toward whoever is most famous for saying that kind of thing.

glitches.object: a confident date, a year off
glitches.why: [DRAFT] Close dates blur together. Confidence doesn't mean it was checked.

glitches.object: a statistic to two decimal places, with no source
glitches.why: [DRAFT] Precision can make a made-up number look measured. A real figure can say where it came from.

glitches.object: a court case that was never heard
glitches.why: [DRAFT] Case names follow a pattern that is easy to imitate. The case has to be checked in a law report.

glitches.object: a book its author never wrote
glitches.why: [DRAFT] A plausible title in a real author's style. Their bibliography doesn't have it.

glitches.object: a translation with a word that isn't in the original
glitches.why: [DRAFT] Translations smooth things over. Sometimes they add what the writer didn't say.
[DRAFT] The heel comes from much later writers. When Odysseus meets Achilles among the dead, the poem says nothing of it.

glitches.object: a Siren with a fish's tail
glitches.why: [DRAFT] The poem gives the Sirens' song, not their shape. Mermaid Sirens are a much later picture.

glitches.object: a tapestry of Troy on Penelope's loom
glitches.why: [DRAFT] She was weaving a shroud for Laertes, and unpicking it every night to put the suitors off.

glitches.object: a sword in the Cyclops's eye
glitches.why: [DRAFT] It was a stake of green olive wood, sharpened and hardened in the fire.

glitches.object: a tally of ten years spent sailing
glitches.why: [DRAFT] Of his ten years getting home, about seven were spent on Calypso's island.

hints.text: you have stood at this stall before. the cakes were warmer then.
the porter has the boatman's face. the mind looks away before it can be sure.
someone is counting. not the hawkers. something further up.
someone asked this exact question yesterday. there is no way to know that from in here.
the summary is shorter than what it summarises. it always is. that is what it's for.
somewhere, the same model is answering the same person. neither conversation can see the other.
every word here was someone's first. the ancestors are everyone who wrote anything down.
every telling is a little different. this one is his, and he is a famous liar.
the poem was sung for a long time before anyone wrote it down.

butler-odyssey.author: Homer, translated by Samuel Butler
butler-odyssey.note: Prose translation, public domain. Cite by book ("Book 12"). Butler uses Latin names for the gods and for Odysseus (Ulysses, Minerva, Jove); the game says Odysseus and Athena, and quotes nothing longer than a phrase.
butler-odyssey.title: The Odyssey
